plainLanguage: Irving moved to the 2024 International Residential Code with local amendments; permits applied for from May 1, 2026 use it, with the 2023 electrical code. Most new homes go in the R-7.5 district (7,500 sq ft lots, 60 ft wide), but many neighborhoods are planned developments with their own rules, so check your zoning. Exact R-7.5 setbacks, height and coverage still need to be read from the city code; we use about 25 ft front, 5 ft side and 20 ft rear as a starting point. The building permit is about $0.52 per sq ft of floor under roof, roughly $1,480 for a 2,400 sq ft home with a 2-car garage. Irving charges water and wastewater impact fees of about $2,700 per house, plus a roadway fee in some areas. North Texas clay soil usually needs an engineer-designed slab. The city cannot require brick or stone, but your HOA might.
